plumbing.review:
- **[P2] A retry can restore the previous run’s commands.** [live.go:689](repo/internal/dashboard/live.go:689) includes commands whenever the step is not ended. But [live.go:774](repo/internal/dashboard/live.go:774) selects the newest existing transcript and assigns it the current step’s `Since`. The factory publishes that new `Since` before creating the replacement directory ([factory.go:2018](repo/internal/factory/factory.go:2018)). During that interval, old commands reappear under the new step, violating the replacement-clearing requirement. Bind private command eligibility to the current run. Add a regression that updates status **before** creating its transcript; the acceptance test currently does the reverse ([act_shell_accept_test.go:402](repo/internal/dashboard/act_shell_accept_test.go:402)).

The patch otherwise stays within the seven authorized files. Acceptance sources match the ratified plan, and [tests.txt:1](tests.txt:1) reports all checks passing. I found no test special-casing, weakened Access checks, added command execution or external requests, public command leakage, or material style mismatch. Commands render through `textContent` ([app.js:1993](repo/internal/dashboard/web/app.js:1993)). The page acceptance test explicitly covers initial HTML only, not browser lifecycle behavior ([act_shell_page_accept_test.go:15](repo/internal/dashboard/act_shell_page_accept_test.go:15)).

As explicitly assigned to the merger, the private-retention exception still needs its recorded decision and a citation on [SPEC.md:135](repo/SPEC.md:135).

VERDICT: changes needed — prevent previous-run command restoration and test that transition; the merger must record and cite the required decision.
